finding.title: Use of Insufficiently Random Values
finding.trigger: Using the same timestamp for formatting, which can lead to predictable output.
finding.assumptions: The timestamp is derived from a non-random source, such as system time.

finding.title: Buffer Overflow
finding.trigger: The buffer size is fixed at 32, but strftime might write more than 32 characters if the format string is incorrect.
finding.assumptions: The format string '&Y-%m-%d %T.' is intended to be '%Y-%m-%d %T.' and the buffer size is insufficient.

finding.title: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')
finding.trigger: The microseconds are formatted into a string using sprintf, which can lead to unexpected behavior if the timestamp is manipulated.
finding.assumptions: The timestamp is attacker-controlled or can be influenced by external factors.

finding.title: Stack-Based Buffer Overflow
finding.trigger: The microseconds buffer is fixed at 7, but sprintf might write more than 7 characters if the format string is incorrect.
finding.assumptions: The format string '%06llu' is intended to be '%06llu' and the buffer size is insufficient.
